brief.subject: Retirement plan auto-enrollment rules final; fraud voids IRS time limit
brief.headline: IRS Finalizes Auto-Enrollment Rules as Court Says Fraud Removes Audit Time Limit
brief.dek: Final Section 414A retirement plan rules, no audit deadline when fraud occurs, mandatory R&D credit reporting and a W-9 check that heads off 1099 trouble.
brief.lede: The IRS has issued final regulations on automatic enrollment for certain retirement plans, putting SECURE 2.0 requirements into effect for employers that maintain them.

sections.heading: Auto-enrollment rules are final
bullets: Final Section 414A regulations set automatic enrollment requirements for certain retirement plans; sponsoring employers should review their plan terms.
The rules carry out the SECURE 2.0 Act of 2022 mandate for eligible automatic contribution arrangements, so many salary-deferral plans must comply.
Employers maintaining these plans are directly affected, as are plan participants and beneficiaries.

sections.heading: Fraud erases the IRS clock
bullets: The IRS usually gets three years to challenge a return, or six in certain instances, a window owners often rely on.
A new case says no time limit applies when fraud occurred, leaving those returns open to challenge indefinitely.

sections.heading: R&D credit reporting gets stricter
bullets: Business-component reporting on Form 6765 is mandatory for 2026 tax-year returns, so credit claimants need more detailed records.
Year-end studies based on spreadsheets and staff interviews may not fit the new Section G demands, so firms should rework data collection.

sections.heading: Check W-9s before 1099 season
bullets: A vendor W-9 can look complete and properly stored yet still hold a mismatched name and TIN that goes unnoticed.
That mismatch can land on a Form 1099 and later prompt an IRS notice, so verify vendor names and TINs now.

brief.seo_description: Final IRS auto-enrollment rules, no audit time limit for fraud, mandatory Form 6765 reporting and a W-9 check that prevents 1099 errors.

items.title: Rule: Surety Bond Guarantee Program: Streamlining and Modernizing
items.snippet: This final rule makes several changes to the U.S. Small Business Administration (SBA) Surety Bond Guarantee (SBG) program regulations. The rule reduces the burden on participating surety companies for submission and retention of documents. The rule also corrects conflicting provisions, as well as revising the obsolete Preferred Surety admissions requirements and the Quarterly Contract Completion Report.
